chunks.title: 1. Requirement & Objective
chunks.heading: WFX ERP › 1. Requirement & Objective
chunks.text:
Business Requirement
We are providing a functionality to combine Styles. For example, a Sales Order contains two Packs built on the same Style — Pack 1 on Style 1 and Pack 2 on Style 1 — MRP will generate for all the Packs added into Sales Order. At MRP event Style level -1 indent will be created as a clubbed requirement against the Sales Order which will lead to create one production Order for a Style.
User visibility is provided at MRP level through two tabs — Kit Demand and MRP — so that the planner can see the KIT/Pack demand and the resulting Style and Raw Material requirement, and thereby plan the requirement more accurately.
Objective
Planning in WFX is done at Style level, not at KIT/Pack level. The objective is therefore to enhance MRP so that a KIT/Pack Sales Order is exploded down to its constituent Styles and Raw Materials, and the requirement is planned at Style level — clubbing Packs that share the same Style into a single consolidated Style requirement. Accordingly, the Production Order (PO) is raised at Style level, one per distinct Style, while the Job Order (JO) is generated for KIT/Pack.
Use Case / Business Scenario
• A KIT (KIT-364) is made up of two different Styles — Style 1 (Flannel Pants) and Style 2 (Flannel LS Shirt). Sales Order for KIT: 1,000 Qty.

chunks.title: Solution Overview
chunks.heading: WFX ERP › 3. Proposed Solution › Solution Overview
chunks.text:
WFX will enhance the Pending MRP List screen so that KIT and Pack Sales Orders are visible as demand and are exploded to Style level, where planning is actually carried out. A new Kit Demand tab will show the KIT/Pack at Level ‑1, where the planner can select and club Packs that are built on the same Style so they are planned as one consolidated requirement rather than Pack by Pack. The resulting requirement is shown on a new MRP tab, which lists the Styles that make up the selected KIT/Packs (Level 1) and the Raw Materials those Styles consume (Level 2) — giving the planner clear visibility of the full requirement before any document is raised.
The Job Order (JO) is generated at KIT/Pack level — running MRP on the KIT/Pack directly creates its Job Order. The Production Orders (PO) are generated at Style level, one per distinct Style contained in the KIT/Pack. For a Pack, which holds two or more units of the same Style, this results in a single PO. For a KIT such as KIT-364, which holds Style 1 (Flannel Pants) and Style 2 (Flannel LS Shirt), this results in two POs — one per Style. Where Packs have been clubbed, the Style-level PO carries the clubbed quantity.
